Assuming decay control is handled by the ![$g_{i}$](https://caml.music.mcgill.ca/~gary/307/week6/img43.png) coefficients, this matrix should be “lossless”. - To achieve frequency-dependent decay control, the ![$g_{i}$](https://caml.music.mcgill.ca/~gary/307/week6/img43.png) coefficients can be replaced by low-order digital filters. - The “tonal correction” filter ![$E(z)$](https://caml.music.mcgill.ca/~gary/307/week6/img44.png) is a low-order filter which serves to equalize modal energy amongst the three bands. - The delay-line lengths are generally chosen to be mutually prime. System “tuning” remains a manual, trial and error process. - A relatively intuitive approach to the building of an FDN reverberator is provided by [Geraint Luff](https://signalsmith-audio.co.uk/writing/2021/lets-write-a-reverb/). - A Matlab Toolbox for developing FDN reverberators is provided by [Sebastian Schlecht](https://github.com/SebastianJiroSchlecht/fdnToolbox). * * * | | | | --- | --- | | [![McGill](https://caml.music.mcgill.ca/~gary/307/images/mcgill.gif)](http://www.mcgill.ca/) | ©2004-2025 McGill University. ## Gloria Dal Santo, Karolina Prawda, Sebastian J. Schlecht, and Vesa Välimäki | ### Demo page for the paper submitted to EURASIP Journal on Audio, Speech, and Music Processing, Directions of DAFx. #### This page includes sound samples of the tested FDN configurations. The samples are divided into three reverberation conditions: lossless, homogeneous decay, frequency-dependent decay. The samples were used in the subjective assessment section of the paper. #### - DiffFDN-O: Optimized differentiable FDN with a random orthogonal feedback matrix. - DiffFDN-RO: DiffFDN with random parameters. These random parameters are used as the initialization for the optimization of DiffFDN. - DiffFDN-SCAT: Optimized differentiable FDN with a scattering feedback matrix. - DiffFDN-HH: Optimized differentiable FDN with a Householder feedback matrix. - SH: FDN implementation of the Schroeder series all-pass reverberator. - REF: Reference (WGN / decaying WGN / FDN with 64 delay lines). ###### Lossless | | | | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | ### N | ### DiffFDN | ### RO | ### DiffFDN (SCAT) | ### DiffFDN (HH) | ### SH | ### REF | | 4 | | | | | | | | 6 | | | | | | | | 8 | | | | | | | ###### Homogeneous Decay | | | | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | ### N | ### DiffFDN | ### RO | ### DiffFDN (SCAT) | ### DiffFDN (HH) | ### SH | ### REF | | 4 | | | | | | | | 6 | | | | | | | | 8 | | | | | | | ###### Frequency Dependent Decay | | | | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | ### DiffFDN | ### RO | ### DiffFDN (SCAT) | ### DiffFDN (HH) | ### SH | ### REF | | N = 4 | | | | | | | | N = 6 | | | | | | | | N = 8 | | | | | | | . _Last updated: 02.02.2024_
